# Draft remote-code declaration

Working material for [#40](https://github.com/foodelevator/scriptsmith/issues/40); reconcile it with the release candidate before submission.

**Does the extension use remotely hosted code? Yes.** We disclose JavaScript generated by OpenAI and JavaScript imported by the user because neither is in the submitted package.

Saved code is registered with `chrome.userScripts.register()`/`update()` and can run immediately with `chrome.userScripts.execute()`. AI-generated live diagnostics also use `userScripts.execute()`, limited to an explicit tab and frame in the editing window whose exact origin the user already approved. All run in the default `USER_SCRIPT` world.

No arbitrary code is passed to `eval`, `Function`, a remote `<script>`, or `chrome.scripting.executeScript`; the latter injects only the packaged element picker. The User Scripts API exception is claimed solely for code it executes. All other extension logic is packaged. Because AI-generated source originates remotely, we disclose it and leave alignment with the API's intended purpose to Chrome Web Store review.

Evidence: [source-to-execution summary and sink inventory](user-script-execution.md).
